The fluorescent lights of the office hummed with the same energy as the panic rising in Dave’s chest. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Dave had made a critical error in judgment: he had brought Barnaby, his African Grey parrot, who possessed not just a voice, but a photographic memory for corporate secrets.

Barnaby sat on his perch, preening a feather, while Dave frantically tried to block the bird’s view of the conference room where the quarterly earnings report was being discussed.

"Good morning, Dave!" chirped Barnaby, his voice a perfect, terrifying replica of the CEO’s. "And remember, the Q3 projections are a complete fabrication. We’re actually bankrupt."

Dave froze. He looked around. The entire open-plan office had gone silent. Sarah from Accounting dropped her stapler.

"Uh, Barnaby," Dave said, sweating profusely. "That’s... that’s a new song. A very avant-garde jazz piece."

Barnaby tilted his head. "Jazz? No. It’s the truth. Also, Dave, you stole the printer toner. And you’re wearing mismatched socks."

Dave looked down. He was.

"Cover him up!" Dave hissed to his intern, Kevin, who was staring at the bird with wide, horrified eyes. "Use the... the plant! The fern!"

Kevin scrambled over, grabbing a potted fern and shoving it over Barnaby’s cage. But Barnaby was resilient. He poked his head out from behind the leaves.

"Kevin," the parrot said, mimicking the voice of the Head of HR. "Your performance review is in five minutes. And you’re still using the company credit card to buy cat food."

Kevin turned pale. "I thought that was a business expense!"

"It’s not!" Barnaby squawked. "Also, Dave, tell me what tool you use to clean your teeth."

The office erupted in confused murmurs. Dave’s brain short-circuited. This was clearly a trap. A corporate espionage trap. If he answered, he might be admitting to something. If he didn’t answer, he looked guilty.

"I... uh..." Dave stammered, backing away slowly. "It’s a... a secret! A proprietary dental technology!"
